research_question: In older adults (≥55 years) with an anxiety or related disorder, does cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) differ from minimal management (waiting list, usual care, supportive/attention control, or medication without active psychological therapy) in dropout/discontinuation rates at 3–6 months post-treatment follow-up?
control_label: Minimal management (waiting list, usual care, supportive/attention control, or medication only)
outcome_description: Dropout/discontinuation (study or treatment attrition) measured at a 3–6 month post-treatment follow-up assessment, expressed as number of dropout events and total randomised participants per arm. Dropout counts should be taken from narrative Results/Attrition/Sample-selection text as well as tables and flow diagrams; where a paper reports two explicitly stated sequential intervals (e.g. n lost by post-treatment plus n further lost by 6 months), these stated numbers are summed to give the cumulative total. If several eligible follow-up points fall within the 3–6 month window, the latest one is used. Immediate post-treatment-only dropout is not eligible.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR > 1, or positive Hedges g on the underlying scale) means MORE dropout/discontinuation in the CBT arm than in the minimal-management arm at 3–6 months post-treatment; values below the null indicate better retention with CBT.

inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in adults with a mean or minimum age around 55 years or older who have an anxiety or related disorder (e.g. GAD, panic, phobia, social anxiety, OCD, PTSD, mixed anxiety, subthreshold/clinically significant worry)

Compares cognitive behavioural therapy (or a clearly CBT-based intervention, any format or delivery mode) with a minimal-management condition such as waiting list, usual/treatment-as-usual care, supportive or attention control, psychoeducation-only, or medication without active psychological therapy
Reports quantitative participant retention or attrition information (dropout counts, completers, or flow data) that includes an assessment point in the 3–6 month post-treatment follow-up window
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, theoretical/commentary paper, or study protocol) or not a randomised controlled trial
No comparison between CBT and a minimal-management control condition (e.g. CBT compared only with another active psychological therapy, or single-arm/uncontrolled design)
No quantitative outcome data allowing effect-size computation (dropout events and per-arm denominators, proportions, or equivalent statistics unavailable)
Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g. younger-adult-only samples, non-anxiety primary condition, or no dropout information at any 3–6 month post-treatment follow-up)
moderators_to_extract: CBT delivery format (individual, group, telephone/internet-guided, self-help)
Type of minimal-management comparator (waiting list vs usual care vs attention/supportive control vs medication only)
Primary anxiety diagnosis (GAD vs mixed/other anxiety vs subthreshold worry)
Length of follow-up interval within the 3–6 month window (months)
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio (RR) of dropout in CBT vs minimal management, using dropout events and total randomised participants per arm. Extract only this outcome; no symptom-severity or other outcomes. Cumulative dropout is the sum of explicitly stated sequential interval counts where a paper reports them that way, and the latest eligible follow-up within 3–6 months is used when multiple are available.
